items.title: Retrieval's bottleneck is moving from finding to selecting
items.reason: Concrete RAG-serving finding from Kapa.ai's own eval: the failure mode shifted from retrieval (finding) to selection -- 34% of gold chunks that search found were never shown to the agentic retriever. Matches 'how models are served' > 'how they are trained'. Single-company benchmark, not independently replicated, but numbers are specific and the mechanism is clearly explained.
key_facts: 18 months ago ~80% of failed eval cases were search misses; now roughly half are selection misses
34% of gold chunks found by search were never passed to the agentic retriever
Pipeline: retrieve 50 chunks, rerank up to 100 with Voyage-3, keep top 15; query decomposition via GPT-6 Luna
Moving top-5 to top-10 chunks raised gold-chunk coverage 14%, with falling precision
Retrieved chunks are ~2/3 of per-query cost in Kapa's assistants
Grep baseline matched deep-retriever recall but only 1-in-25 returned chunks were needed; deep retriever used 8x fewer tokens at ~6x precision

items.title: Hiding Capabilities in AI Models
items.reason: Schneier flags a real paper ('AI Models Can Provably Hide Arbitrary Capabilities') showing a cryptographic-locker backdoor can hide a dangerous capability inside a model's weights such that it survives fine-tuning, weight noising, gradient trigger search, and latent adversarial training -- i.e. elicitation-based safety audits can be made to fail in principle. Concrete PyTorch PoC, not just theory. This directly undercuts the premise of capability evals, which is squarely in the profile's eval-methodology lane.
key_facts: Backdoor = encrypted neural network embedded in host model weights via a 'digital locker' construction, unlocked only by a secret trigger
PoC in PyTorch; stand-in dangerous capability = chemical reaction prediction task (CBRN proxy)
Hidden capability survived fine-tuning, weight noising, gradient-based trigger search, and latent adversarial training
Extends prior work (hiding fixed strings) to arbitrary computation
Commenters raised: can statistical tests detect the embedded network even if it can't be elicited; concern that releasing the PoC models helps attackers too

items.title: OpenAI Compaction Flaw Let Researchers Bypass Hidden Reasoning Protections
items.reason: Real, named PoC: researchers (Xint) smuggled encrypted chain-of-thought out of OpenAI's compaction feature by having the model echo it into the compacted item with space-for-tab substitution, which skipped the cross-model reasoning-reuse check because compaction runs on the same model. OpenAI confirmed and fixed it (Oct 23) and paid a $6,000 bounty -- primary source exists even though this article is secondary reporting.
key_facts: Technique: ask model to copy encrypted reasoning into compacted item, substitute tabs for spaces to dodge policy filters
Exploits a gap where OpenAI's cross-model reasoning-reuse check doesn't fire because compaction runs on the same model that produced the reasoning
Compacted item replayed through gpt-4.1 and gpt-4o, which emitted it as plaintext
Tested against gpt-5.6-sol only; GPT-6 Astra not checked
OpenAI fixed server-side Oct 23, 2026; paid Xint a $6,000 bounty
No confirmation the recovered text is a verbatim match, and no evidence of in-the-wild exploitation

items.title: Fuzzers vs. AI: Comparing Fuzzilli and BigSleep on JavaScript Engines
items.reason: Google Project Zero's own head-to-head of a traditional fuzzer (Fuzzilli) against an AI agent (BigSleep/Gemini 3.6 flash) finding V8 bugs in production, six months of data, with a rediscovery experiment controlling for memorization. This is exactly the kind of primary, numeric, verifiable AI x cyber evaluation the profile wants -- running system, not a description of one.
key_facts: Apr-Sep 2026 production: Fuzzilli 316 total reports / 178 vulnerabilities; BigSleep 441 total / 95 vulnerabilities
Actionable vulnerabilities (deduped, fixed): BigSleep 45 vs Fuzzilli 37 -- roughly a tie
Overlap ~25% (20/81) of actionable reports; a separate experiment estimated ~60% overlap

Rediscovery test: BigSleep found ~62% of 112 historic Fuzzilli-found bugs from the introducing commit, a different bug for ~12% more, nothing on ~26%; follow-up prompting raised relevant-bug rate to ~70%
No significant memorization effect detected for pre-training-cutoff bugs
Overlap smaller for JIT-compiler bugs; bugs hard for the fuzzer tend to be hard for the agent too
Project Zero's conclusion: complementary, run both

items.title: CyberStrikeAI Uses 44 AI Agents to Automate Hacking Operations Against Japan Targets

No PoC or technical detail in this article, 'validation activity' at 19 orgs rather than confirmed breaches, and the Learned rule flags exactly this pattern (named-incident reporting with scary agent framing and no primary technical source) as a repeat reject. Keeping the score modest rather than zero because a named vendor report with checkable specifics is still better than a rumor.
